title: Stow police officer accused of misusing Flock system to track former partner

reading.body:
This is an access-control failure inside a law enforcement deployment. A licensed user of the Flock camera system and of the CJIS and CORI databases is accused of running queries about a person he had previously dated, repeatedly, over two years. The systems were working as designed: they returned location and record information to an authenticated officer. What failed was the assumption that an authenticated officer's queries are legitimate ones.

The misuse happened at the query layer, not in the cameras or the databases themselves. Catching it would have required auditing who searched for whom and why, and comparing that pattern against the officer's own connections. The internal affairs investigation took four weeks and was triggered by the woman's discovery, not by any alert from the systems involved.

The department filed a criminal complaint and found that he had used state systems to obtain information about her. He was placed on paid leave in July and unpaid leave as of July 31, and a Select Board hearing could decide his employment. The criminal complaint is an allegation, not a finding of guilt, and no court has ruled on the state law violations it cites.

reports.title: Stow police officer accused of misusing Flock system to track former partner

summary:
A Stow police officer, Jason Rogers, is accused of misusing police databases to track a woman he previously dated. The woman said she ended the relationship about five years ago, changed her identity, phone number, and social media habits after leaving. She discovered this summer that Rogers had searched for her location through the Flock camera system and other law enforcement databases, including CJIS and CORI, multiple times in 2024 and 2025. She also said he drove by her home.

The Stow Police Department filed a criminal complaint against Rogers on July 17 for potential state law violations. After a four-week internal affairs investigation, the department found he had used state systems to obtain information about the woman. Rogers was placed on paid administrative leave in July, then unpaid leave as of July 31. The woman has a restraining order against him lasting at least a year. A Select Board hearing next week could decide his employment status.
